clue.text: Temperature effect includes possible victim of warming sea

indicators.note: the phrase before it is said to include the answer, so its letters run across the word boundary inside it

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A climate report notes that rising temperatures harm something living in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'temperatuRE EFfect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral reefs bleach and die when ocean water gets too warm, so they are a likely casualty of a heating sea.

clue.text: I'm serious, see what I'm saying?

blocks.note: first meaning: an emphatic insistence that one means it
second meaning: literally, watch my mouth to make out the words

explanation.walkthrough: 'See what I'm saying' usually means 'understand me', but here it is literal: watching the words form on the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'I mean this', and literally an invitation to lip-read the speaker.

clue.text: Former King curtailing speech in Rivendell?

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, so the last letter is removed

blocks.note: Rivendell is the elf haven in Tolkien, where the elves speak their own language

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch interrupts the talk at an elven refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is the King of Rock and Roll, not a Tolkien ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was nicknamed the King of Rock and Roll, and he died in 1977, so he is a past King.

clue.text: Be off to drink a traditional scrumpy — turned, I'm afraid

definitions.note: the definition is what a coward would say, standing in for the coward

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so the first word wraps around what follows
cider that has turned has gone off, but cryptically turning means writing the word backwards

blocks.note: scat is a command to go away
taken as written
the old-fashioned spelling of cider; scrumpy is rough farmhouse cider from the West of England

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave after drinking scrumpy that has gone sour confesses to being nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAT holds A plus CYDER written backwards. The definition is a confession: the person saying 'I'm afraid' is a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaredy-cat is a childish word for a timid person, someone who would readily admit to fear.

clue.text: Discussion about Irish mostly living way up mountain

indicators.note: the discussion goes round the pieces that follow
only most of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a chat is a discussion
IR is the abbreviation for Irish
living is life

explanation.surface: Talk about Irish people mostly living on a mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairlift is a cable-hauled line of seats carrying skiers and walkers up a slope.

clue.text: Her and my playing sound similar at the end

indicators.note: playing about with letters moves them into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of the two pronouns, the 'and' only linking them

explanation.surface: Two people performing music together end on a matching note.
explanation.definitionFit: Words rhyme when their final syllables share a sound, as in 'cat' and 'hat'.

clue.text: One's walked all over Dartmoor, not quite disoriented

indicators.note: not quite all of the word is used, so its last letter goes
something disoriented has lost its bearings, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Dartmoor is a moorland in Devon; its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A hiker has tramped across Dartmoor and is a bit lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is literally trodden on and figuratively a person who lets others exploit them.

clue.text: Cutting of climber almost strangled by my flowering bush

indicators.note: almost the whole word is used, so its final letter is dropped
a strangler's hands close around the neck, so the following pieces surround this one

blocks.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
a rose is a flowering shrub
ivy is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A gardener's cutting from a climbing plant gets choked by their own rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like a plant slip in the gardening picture but is the adjective meaning sharp or biting.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrosive remarks are caustic and wounding, which is what cutting means of words.

clue.text: Projection from mouth that usually stops kiss at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: Something sticking out of the mouth tends to get in the way of a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusk is a long tooth jutting out of an animal's mouth, as on an elephant or walrus.

clue.text: Pressing desire never to lose heart

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, so the central letter is taken out

blocks.note: an urge is a desire
'never' can stand for 'not', as in 'never fear'

explanation.surface: Advice to keep up a strong wish and never get discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing matters are urgent ones, demanding immediate attention.

clue.text: I'll oppose memorable date, making second to fourth day

definitions.note: the definition is what an opponent would say, standing in for the opponent

indicators.note: this says letters two through four of the date are turned into something else

blocks.note: a date marking an event worth remembering
D is the standard abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone vows resistance to moving a commemoration to a different day of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: In ANNIVERSARY the second to fourth letters, NNI, are replaced by D.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary is an opponent, the kind of person who announces resistance to you.

clue.text: Brutes turn over matter to the courts

indicators.note: 'over' asks for the preceding word to be flipped end to end

blocks.note: a turn in a game is a go
res is the Latin legal term for a thing or matter, as in res judicata

explanation.surface: Thugs hand a dispute over to the legal system.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are monstrous giants of folklore, so the word is used for brutal, cruel people.

clue.text: Rubber marks guarantee to bring the end forward

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is moved up ahead of the letters before it

blocks.note: M is short for marks, the old German currency
to assure is to guarantee

explanation.surface: An eraser leaves smudges, a promise to put the conclusion earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of ASSURE jumps forward two places to sit before the UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur rubs clients' muscles, so cryptically he is a rubber, one who rubs.

clue.text: English climate protesters circling low national park

indicators.note: the protesters go round what follows, surrounding it

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
XR is Extinction Rebellion, the climate protest movement
a cow's low is a moo

explanation.surface: Climate activists surround a low-lying English protected landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the cow's call, not an adjective for flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: Exmoor is a moorland area in Somerset and Devon, designated one of England's national parks.

clue.text: One with backbone investing billions in green energy tax

indicators.note: investing money puts it into something, so the billions go inside the rest

blocks.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
E is the symbol for energy
B is the abbreviation for billions
rates were a British local property tax

explanation.surface: A brave person puts billions into a levy on renewable power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with backbone' suggests a courageous person but means a creature with a spine.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertebrate is any animal with a spinal column, literally having a backbone.

clue.text: A coming out that's suddenly shocking?

definitions.text: A coming out that's suddenly shocking?

blocks.clueFragment: A coming out that's suddenly shocking?
blocks.note: surface reading: a surprise revelation of someone's identity

blocks.clueFragment: A coming out that's suddenly shocking?
blocks.note: setter's reading: workers coming out on a walkout called without notice, or a bolt that literally shocks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out' is the trade-union sense, workers coming out on strike; 'shocking' plays on an electrical bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike called without warning is so named, and the phrase is also a literal bolt of electricity hitting the ground.

clue.text: Unusually strong queen dismissing both knights, not a pretty sight

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement is not the normal order, so the letters are reworked
dismissed pieces are sent away, so they leave the fodder

blocks.note: the letters of both words
N is the chess notation for knight; there is one in each word

explanation.surface: A powerful chess queen captures both knights, leaving an ugly position.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the two Ns from STRONG QUEEN, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotesque means comically or repulsively ugly, something no one would call pretty.

clue.text: Diver's remorse, eating endless acidic fruit

indicators.note: with no end, the last letter of the fruit is lost
eating takes food inside, so the remorse surrounds the fruit

blocks.note: guilt is remorse
a lemon is a sour citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A deep-sea diver feels bad about munching a sour fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' is a bird that dives for fish, not a person in scuba gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a seabird of the auk family that dives underwater to catch fish.

clue.text: Anarchic idea of suited office worker, ignoring page weight for Americans

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped from the office worker

blocks.note: proper means suitable
a typist works in an office
P is the abbreviation for page
heft is mainly American for weight

explanation.surface: An office worker in a suit forgets to weigh a page, in American units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suited' is an adjective meaning fitting, not a clothed worker.
explanation.definitionFit: The slogan is Proudhon's famous anarchist claim that private ownership is itself a form of robbery.

clue.text: Was suffering but carried on

blocks.note: first meaning: put up with hardship
second meaning: lasted, continued

explanation.walkthrough: 'But' reads as a contrast, yet the two halves are two senses of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is both to bear pain or hardship and to persist or last over time.

clue.text: Support broken by climbing ladder, holding post

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the word goes backwards
the support is broken open and the other piece is put into the gap

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
a ladder in tights or stockings is a run

explanation.surface: A prop gives way under someone going up a ladder holding a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder in British usage is also a run in hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding of an office or position, or the period during which it is held.

clue.text: Adding any number twice could make this field average lower

indicators.text: Adding any number twice could make this
indicators.note: the answer is what remains before two letters were added, so they come out of the wordplay

blocks.note: the mean is an average
to lower something is to put it down
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A statistics puzzle: doubling a figure could pull the average down for this area.
explanation.walkthrough: Put N into the answer twice and you get MEAN DOWN; so the answer is MEAN DOWN without its two Ns.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, often used for hay.

clue.text: Roll wide part of shoe

blocks.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
the heel is the raised back of a shoe

explanation.surface: An instruction about manipulating a broad section of footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide is a cricket delivery out of the batter's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel something is to roll it along, as with a barrow or trolley.

clue.text: Very old script at hand in library

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: LIB is a common abbreviation for library
something at hand is near

explanation.surface: An ancient manuscript is kept within reach in a library.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear B is the Bronze Age Mycenaean Greek writing system, deciphered by Michael Ventris in 1952.

clue.text: Court helper drops each book in temper

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a ballboy fetches balls on a tennis court
B is the abbreviation for book; 'each' means every B goes

explanation.surface: A tennis assistant loses his cool and throws each book down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' suggests anger but means to moderate by mixing in something else.
explanation.definitionFit: To alloy is to mix a metal with a baser one, hence to temper or dilute something.

clue.text: Crime-solving tool to help when Ben escapes

indicators.note: whatever escapes gets away, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: to benefit someone is to help them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police use a device to help after a prisoner called Ben breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-FIT is a computer-generated likeness of a suspect, built from witness descriptions.

clue.text: Question welcomed by impartial holy man

indicators.note: being welcomed means being taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Q is the abbreviation for question
fair means impartial

explanation.surface: A neutral holy figure is willing to hear a query.
explanation.definitionFit: A faqir, also spelt fakir, is a Muslim or Hindu religious ascetic who lives on alms.

clue.text: De la Mare's tragic heroine from Hugo's book

indicators.note: a tragic turn of events wrecks things, so the name's letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: the poet's name and the possessive s supply all nine letters

clue.text: Die tool fused onto article that measures angles

indicators.note: fused things are melted together into a new form, so these letters are remade

blocks.note: the definite article
these seven letters are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a relative clause standing for 'thing that measures angles'.
explanation.definitionFit: A theodolite is a surveyor's instrument with a rotating telescope for measuring horizontal and vertical angles.

clue.text: Extremely tiny kiddie?

first and last letters
